subject: Clarify: analytics vendor - limited-use carveout vs 'sale' classification
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeanalytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@edgeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Analytics integration - privacy classification questions and DPA redline

Hi Aditya / Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our legal team's review, we have two items that are blocking the DPA signature for the analytics integration: 1) whether the telemetry we collect for product analytics would be treated as a "sale" under CCPA/CPRA or can be governed via a limited-use/service provider carveout; and 2) details on Redwood's subprocessors and whether any telemetry processing may involve cross-border transfers (we need onshore fallback for certain PHI-adjacent flows).

Attached is our redline (EdgeAnalytics_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) and a current list of our subprocessors (subprocessors_list.csv) so you can see what we’ve already contracted with. High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm if Redwood will agree to service-provider-only processing for the analytics event stream and explicit limited-use language (no resale or targeted advertising).
- If certain telemetry must be aggregated/exported to partner services, we'd like to understand whether that constitutes a "sale" or whether it remains covered by the limited-use restrictions.
- Subprocessor attestations and SOC2 evidence for any onshore fallback providers.

Can you point us to the clause you'd accept for limited-use? If Redwood can accept a tight limited-use definition and the subprocessor attestation, we can proceed to countersign. We’re hoping to close this by the end of next week.

Appreciate the help — Samira

--
Samira Khan
Head of Privacy & Compliance, EdgeAnalytics
samira.k@edgeanalytics.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Analytics integration - privacy classification questions and DPA redline

Samira — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the redline and subprocessors list. Quick responses and a proposed path forward below.

1) Limited-use/service-provider vs "sale": Redwood's default position for telemetry and product analytics is to accept a service-provider (processor) model with a narrow limited-use clause that prohibits resale and targeted advertising. Practically, that means we will process events to provide analytics, diagnostics, and feature telemetry back to your tenant and will not sell personal data or use it for advertising.

2) Aggregation and exports: Aggregation for analytics dashboards (e.g., cohort metrics, retention curves) is covered by the limited-use model. If you want us to export PII-rich event payloads to third-party partners (for example a workplace analytics partner), that could trigger "sale" considerations depending on your state law interpretation. We can add explicit language that allows Redwood to export only aggregated/non-identifiable derivatives to partners — any raw PII exports would need prior written consent or a separate scope.

3) Subprocessors and onshore fallback: We can provide attestations for our primary subprocessors; for onshore fallback we use a partner (OnshoreProxy LLC) and can produce SOC2 reports or an attestation letter. Please let us know which categories you consider PHI-adjacent so we can map the exact flow.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura, can you review the attached redline and propose a short acceptable paragraph we can offer that covers limited-use, exports, and the non-resale guarantee?
- Samira, if you send the list of PHI-adjacent event types (or examples), Naomi and I will map them to subprocessors and provide the SOC2/attestation artifacts.

Timing: we can provide the artifacts and a proposed paragraph by EOD Friday (23 Apr) if that works.

Regards,
Aditya
Director, Customer Integrations
Redwood Inference

+1 650-555-0123

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Analytics integration - privacy classification questions and DPA redline

Thanks Aditya — that approach sounds promising. Per your ask, attached is a short list of events we deem PHI-adjacent (examples only): session_error_stack_traces (may include user-submitted notes), support_ticket_comments (some contain health context), and form_payloads from our intake flow.

We can accept aggregated exports to partners if they are irreversible and de-identified per NIST guidance; raw event payload exports will need explicit prior written approval.

I uploaded the updated subprocessors CSV to the Drive link and sent a DocuSign envelope for the current redline (see link below). If Redwood can accept a narrow limited-use clause along the lines you described and confirm SOC2/attestation for the OnshoreProxy fallback, I think procurement will greenlight signature.

On the timeline — end of next week is tight but doable if we get the attestation artifacts and a short paragraph for the DPA by Friday.

Best,
Samira

--

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@edgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Analytics integration - privacy classification questions and DPA redline

Hi Samira — thanks for the event list and the quick turnaround. Laura from Legal here (copying Naomi for operations mapping).

We reviewed your redline and propose the following compromise paragraph for insertion into Section 2 (Processing Scope):

"Redwood will process Customer Personal Data solely as a Service Provider on behalf of Customer and solely for the purposes of (i) delivering analytics and diagnostics to Customer; (ii) improving Redwood's services in a de-identified and aggregated form; and (iii) performing security, fraud prevention, and legal compliance activities. Redwood shall not sell Customer Personal Data or use Customer Personal Data for targeted advertising. Redwood may export aggregated, irreversible derivatives to third-party partners provided such outputs do not permit re-identification; any export of raw, PII-containing event payloads to third-party partners requires prior written consent from Customer."

Additionally:
- We will provide the SOC2 report for OnshoreProxy LLC under NDA and will add a subprocessor attestation clause to the DPA that requires notification and a right to object for material changes.
- For the PHI-adjacent event types you listed, we will configure an onshore-only processing path; Naomi will follow up with the operational mapping and estimated cutover timeline (target: 3 business days after countersignature).

Attached is an updated DPA addendum (RI_DPA_addendum_aditya_20270425.pdf) with the proposed paragraph and the subprocessor attestation language tracked. If that looks acceptable, please sign the DocuSign and we’ll provide the SOC2 for OnshoreProxy under the NDA link.

If you want any tweaks to the limited-use text, flag them in the DocuSign comments and we’ll try to accommodate quickly.

Thanks — Laura
